title: Medical emergencies can lead to debt and bankruptcy — even for insured Americans
titleZh: 一场意外，足以让有医保的美国人跌出安全区
summary:
即便是拥有医疗保险的美国人，在遭遇突发医疗事件后，仍可能背负长期的财务压力。《健康事务》期刊本月发表的一项研究显示，在因车祸、跌倒等创伤性事故住院后的18个月内，医疗债务进入催收程序的患者比例，较事故发生前上升了5.2个百分点，相对增幅达24%。在同一伤后观察期内，这些患者的人均被催收债务额增加了290美元，每10名负债者中就有1人欠款超过4480美元。

来源：CNBC；作者：Annie Nova；原文发布时间：2026-02-19 20:00:00

paragraphs.contentEn: Even Americans who are covered by health insurance can emerge from medical emergencies with long-lasting financial scars. In a study published this month in the journal Health Affairs, researchers found that 18 months after being hospitalized for a traumatic injury — such as a car accident or fall — the share of patients with medical debt in collections rose 5.2 percentage points, or a 24% relative increase, compared with before that medical emergency. Over that same period post-injury, the average balance in collections rose by $290, and 1 in 10 indebted patients owed more than $4,480.
paragraphs.contentZh: 即便是拥有医疗保险的美国人，在遭遇突发医疗事件后，仍可能背负长期的财务压力。《健康事务》期刊本月发表的一项研究显示，在因车祸、跌倒等创伤性事故住院后的18个月内，医疗债务进入催收程序的患者比例，较事故发生前上升了5.2个百分点，相对增幅达24%。在同一伤后观察期内，这些患者的人均被催收债务额增加了290美元，每10名负债者中就有1人欠款超过4480美元。

paragraphs.contentEn: The researchers studied nearly 13,000 trauma patients’ credit reports from one year before to 18 months after they were hospitalized for an injury. Credit report data spanned 2018-2021. Nearly all the patients in the cohort — or 98% — had health insurance coverage. “Insurance reduces the risk of financial catastrophe, but the way private plans are currently designed still leaves many people heavily exposed when something serious happens,” Scott said.
paragraphs.contentZh: 研究人员分析了近1.3万名创伤患者的信用报告，时间跨度涵盖其因伤住院前一年至住院后18个月。所有信用数据的时间范围为2018年至2021年。在这批研究对象中，几乎所有人（占98%）都拥有医疗保险。斯科特表示：“医疗保险确实能够降低个人陷入财务灾难的风险，但按照目前私人医保计划的设计，一旦发生严重事故，仍有许多人会面临沉重的经济负担。”

paragraphs.contentEn: The study’s findings come at a time when health costs are a strain for many Americans, even among broader affordability worries. According to a recent poll by KFF, a nonpartisan health policy research group, two-thirds of Americans surveyed, or 66%, are worried about paying for health care — more than other household necessities such as utilities, food and groceries, housing and rent.
paragraphs.contentZh: 这项研究发布之际，医疗费用正给许多美国人带来沉重压力，即使在普遍的生活成本焦虑中，医疗账单带来的负担也格外突出。无党派健康政策研究机构KFF近期公布的一项民调显示，三分之二（66%）的受访美国人表示担心无力承担医疗费用——这一比例超过了对水电、食品杂货、房租等家庭基本开支的担忧。

paragraphs.contentEn: While the ACA expanded health insurance coverage to millions of Americans, many private plans come with high deductibles that require people pay thousands of dollars before their insurance takes effect, Scott said. In 2026, the average marketplace deductible is $5,304 for a silver plan and $7,186 for a bronze plan, KFF found. “An unexpected injury can mean thousands of dollars in out-of-pocket costs before insurance pays a dime,” Scott said.
paragraphs.contentZh: 斯科特指出，尽管《平价医疗法案》让数百万美国人获得了医保，但许多私人保险计划仍设有较高的免赔额，在保险开始报销前，个人往往需要先自行支付数千美元。KFF的数据显示，2026年医保市场银级计划的平均免赔额达5304美元，铜级计划为7186美元。斯科特补充道：“一次意外受伤，可能意味着在保险真正开始支付费用之前，当事人就必须先承担数千美元的自付开销。”

paragraphs.contentEn: Caitlin Donovan, senior director at the National Patient Advocate Foundation, said it was disturbing to see, in the study, “the utter failure of private insurance to protect people from debt and bankruptcy.” “This study highlighted the need to build more protections into private insurance, either by limiting deductibles or even building in income-based limitations on out-of-pocket spending,” she said.
paragraphs.contentZh: 全美患者权益倡导基金会高级总监凯特琳·多诺万表示，这项研究结果令人不安，因为它揭示了“私人保险在保护民众免于陷入债务和破产方面存在明显不足”。她进一步指出：“研究结果凸显，有必要在私人保险制度中引入更多保障措施，例如设定免赔额上限，或建立与收入挂钩的自付费用封顶机制。”

paragraphs.contentEn: Trauma patients on Medicare and Medicaid saw different outcomes, with minimal changes in medical debt and bankruptcy later on, the researchers found. That was likely because Medicaid has minimal out-of-pocket costs, while expenses on Medicare are often capped, Scott said. “If insurance is supposed to protect you from financial ruin after a health shock, Medicaid did its job,” Scott said. “Private insurance, for many people, did not.”
paragraphs.contentZh: 研究人员发现，参与联邦医疗保险或医疗补助计划的创伤患者情况则截然不同，其后续医疗债务与破产发生率变化不大。斯科特解释称，这可能是因为医疗补助计划的自付费用极低，而联邦医疗保险通常也设有患者自付额度的上限。斯科特表示：“如果说保险的职责是在健康危机后防止个人陷入财务困境，那么医疗补助发挥了应有的作用。但对许多人来说，私人保险并未实现这一目标。”

Bankruptcy filings also increased by 3.2 per 1,000 patients — a 6% relative rise — about 15 months after injury, the researchers found. “This work grew out of my clinical experience as a trauma surgeon and seeing acutely injured patients shouting at us to stop care because they’re worried about the bill,” said co-author Dr. John Scott, an associate professor of surgery at the University of Washington.
研究人员还发现，受伤约15个月后，每千名患者中申请破产的人数增加了3.2人，相对增幅达6%。该研究的合著者、华盛顿大学外科副教授约翰·斯科特表示：“这项研究的灵感源于我作为创伤外科医生的临床经历，我曾目睹一些伤势严重的患者，因担心医疗账单，不停冲我们喊停治疗。”

Legislators let the enhanced subsidies on the Affordable Care Act marketplace expire at the end of 2025, which is expected to create a surge of uninsured Americans and others with higher deductibles before their health coverage kicks in. “If people are pushed into thinner coverage or out of coverage entirely, those numbers will only get worse,” Scott said of the financial impact of sustaining an injury.
立法者已决定让《平价医疗法案》（ACA）医保市场的额外补贴在2025年底到期，这一变化预计将导致无保险人群增加，同时也会让更多参保者在医保开始报销前面临更高的自付免赔额。谈及受伤后的财务影响时，斯科特表示：“如果人们被迫转向保障更低的保险计划，甚至完全失去保险，这些数字只会进一步恶化。”
